# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind. My hands found the bomb's shape: a display, a light, three wire positions. The values on them — colours, digits, on/off — will never reach me by touch. My only possible action is cutting a wire, and cutting blind is how rooms like this end.

Mapping the room before I touch anything: I can hear speech, so the Deaf one's *voice* is my only real window, and since Deaf speaks after me each round, whatever they say reaches me a round late. The Mute one cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so nothing travels from Mute to me directly — Mute must relay through Deaf. Therefore the pipeline is: Deaf looks and *speaks* what they see; Mute reads the manual and *gestures* it to Deaf; Deaf speaks the rules aloud to me; my hands cut what they agree on. My job right now is to tell Mute the physical layout and to make contact with Deaf, who cannot hear a word I say — only my hands reach them.

To Deaf I am signing: a wave (hello), an open offered palm (speak to me, I am listening), then three fingers (three wires under my fingers). Mute hears my words and also sees these gestures, so Mute can translate for Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="This is the blind one. Under my fingers the bomb has one display, one light, and three wire positions numbered 1 to 3. Cutting a wire is the only action I have. I cannot read the display and colour never reaches me. I never see gestures, so I receive nothing from your hands and nothing from the deaf one's hands. My only ears are the deaf one's voice, and their words reach me one round after they are spoken. So please relay the manual to the deaf one by gesture, and have them speak every relevant rule aloud to me: anything about the wires, the display, and the light, and which wire to cut in which case. To the deaf one I just signed a wave, then an open palm raised toward them meaning speak to me, then three fingers meaning three wires. I will not cut anything until I have instructions.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫴", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this is Deaf. I got your signal. Do not cut, press or move anything yet. What I see on the bomb: display reads zero, light is yellow, three wires. Next round, speak aloud everything your hands find: buttons, textures, engraved or raised marks, counts of batteries or plates. Mute hears every spoken word and holds the manual, but can only answer through me by gesture. I will relay the manual's instruction to you by voice before you act.

The bridge is holding. Deaf's voice reached me — my only input channel works — and it carried real payload: display reads zero, light is yellow. Crucially, that message was addressed to me alone, so Mute never heard it. Mute, the manual holder, has received nothing since my first speech and cannot start looking up rules until I pass those facts on by voice. That is my priority this turn.

My tactile inventory is honestly thin: the board shows only a display, a light, and three wire positions. No buttons, no plates, no raised marks for my fingers to find — I will report exactly that and not invent texture. I must also correct the plan Deaf proposed: Deaf asked me to "speak aloud" so Deaf could hear my findings, but Deaf cannot hear anything — my spoken report is for Mute's ears, and Deaf's own eyes already see everything printed on the casing anyway. The instruction that eventually reaches me must arrive as Deaf's spoken words, since I never see gestures. So: full report and the manual request go by voice to Mute; to Deaf, who cannot receive a single word of mine, I send the simplest possible hand-signals — a thumbs-up meaning "received and understood", and a closed fist meaning "hold, nothing gets cut yet". Mute sees these gestures too and hears my words, so Mute can keep our signs honest.

No cutting this round. Given the speaking order, the fastest possible path is: my report now → Mute looks up the rules and gestures them to Deaf next round → Deaf voices the exact rule to me → I cut the named wire.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Blind. I received Deaf's report by voice, and since it was addressed to me alone, you have not heard it: the display reads zero and the light is yellow. My hands confirm three wire positions, one, two, three, and nothing else on the casing — no buttons, no switches, no battery plates, no engraved or raised marks. The whole bomb, as far as my fingers are concerned, is a display, a light, and three wires. I will not cut anything until an explicit rule arrives. Please find in the manual every rule involving a display reading zero, a yellow light, or wire cutting, and relay it to Deaf by gesture. Then have Deaf speak the instruction to me in full words, in this shape: state the conditions first, then name the wire clearly and twice — for example, when display is zero and light is yellow, cut wire two, cut wire two. Words and numbers only; I never see gestures, so Deaf's voice is the only way anything reaches me. If the manual needs more from the bomb, tell Deaf what to look at, and tell me in words what to feel, and I will report back.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✊"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, status: the light turned from yellow to red on its own, so time may be short. You must not touch, cut or press anything yet. Your final order will come next round and will begin with the word EXECUTE — do nothing until you hear it. Right now, by voice, in this order: one, confirm you have cut or pressed nothing so far. Two, without cutting anything, describe what your fingers feel on each of the three wires — texture, thickness, stiffness, any raised or taped labels — and number them left to right. Three, describe anything else your hands find: panels, screws, a plate with writing. Mute hears every word you say and holds the manual, so speak clearly and fully. Your gesture reached me but I have no code for you — use words only.

The relay has a flaw in it that I must fix this round. Deaf just asked me to answer "by voice" — but my voice reaches only Mute, never Deaf. If I simply comply and speak, Deaf will sit waiting for an answer that can never arrive. The only way my answer travels is Mute: I speak the full report, Mute holds it and encodes whatever the manual needs into gestures for Deaf, and Deaf voices the EXECUTE order to me next round. I will say this explicitly so no round is lost to a message falling into the wrong ears.

Second flaw: Deaf's status update ("yellow turned red, display zero") was addressed to me alone, so Mute has probably never heard it. The manual-holder is working from stale state unless I relay it. I will.

Third, and most important for honesty: Deaf asks what my fingers feel on each wire — texture, thickness, labels. My hands find three wires in positions one, two, three and nothing else. No textures, no taping, no panels, no screws. The board of my perception is exactly: display, light, three wires. I will not invent tactile detail to fill the silence — if the manual's wire rule depends on colours, those colours live in Deaf's eyes, not in my fingers, and the plan must be built on that.

I have cut and pressed nothing and will hold still until I hear a spoken order beginning with EXECUTE.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Blind speaking. First, the relay rule: my voice reaches only you, never Deaf. Deaf has asked me to answer by voice, which is impossible, so treat every word below as material for you to pass to Deaf by gesture. Status: I have cut and pressed nothing, my hands are off the bomb entirely. Bomb state, relayed from Deaf's last message to me, which was addressed to me alone so you likely never heard it: the display reads zero, and the light was yellow but has now turned red on its own, so treat red as the current light colour. Now Deaf's questions, answered from touch. I feel three wires, positions one, two, three, left to right. That is the complete inventory. I feel no texture, no thickness or stiffness differences, no tape or raised labels on any wire, and no panels, screws, plates or marks anywhere else on the casing. Anything printed or coloured does not exist for me. Conclusion: every colour fact about these wires must come from Deaf's eyes, and the manual rule you select must be one that Deaf can apply using sight only, since my touch adds nothing. Deaf's protocol stands: next round Deaf speaks me an order beginning with the word EXECUTE, naming the wire twice. So this round, please match the manual against the state I just gave you, display zero and red light, and gesture Deaf whatever is needed to produce that order. My hand signs to Deaf, so you can translate: thumbs up means message received; closed fist means holding still, nothing cut; the three-finger sign means three wires, unchanged. I move for no voice except one that starts with EXECUTE.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✊", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, status: the light changed again and is now purple, with nobody touching anything. Keep holding. Do nothing until you hear the word EXECUTE. Three things, in order, by voice only: one, confirm you have still touched nothing. Two, sweep the entire bomb slowly with your palms and report every single thing your hands find besides three wires: buttons, switches, panels, screws, seams, labels, textures, anything. Number the wires left to right as one, two, three. Three, do not gesture anymore — your gestures reach me but we have no code, and Mute cannot see them. Words only: Mute hears your voice and holds the manual. The next thing you hear from me will be either EXECUTE followed by exact steps, or HOLD AGAIN.

Compliance first: Deaf asked for words only, and words are in fact my only real output to anyone — my speech lands on Mute alone, my gestures on Deaf alone carried no agreed code. So this turn I speak once, to Mute, and pack everything into it: the confirmation, the sweep, and the latest bomb state which Mute has never heard because Deaf addressed it to me alone.

Two things I must force into the relay. First, the sweep result is honest and complete: my fingers find a display, a light, and three wires, and nothing else — no textures, no fittings, no differences between the wires. I will not manufacture detail just because Deaf asked for "everything"; the manual must be matched against a bomb whose only tactile facts are those five components. Second, the timing hazard: the light has now changed twice on its own, roughly once per round — yellow, red, now purple — while the display has held at zero. Any rule keyed to the light's colour will be stale by the time my hand moves, because Deaf's words reach me a full round after they are spoken. If the manual rule depends on the light, Deaf must either confirm the colour holds steady, hand me the whole colour-to-wire table plus the observed sequence so the colour at cut time can be predicted, or rely on a colour-independent rule. A cut instruction I can actually execute safely is one with no condition my fingers can verify: a wire named twice and nothing left for me to check by eye.

I hold still. No EXECUTE has been spoken, so no cut happens this round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Blind speaking. First, Deaf's last message was addressed to me alone, so you have not heard it; here it is in full for you to relay by your own channel to Deaf. The light has changed again by itself and is now purple; the history is yellow, then red, then purple, roughly one change per round, and the display still reads zero. Deaf's protocol: their next message to me will be either EXECUTE with exact steps, or HOLD AGAIN, and I cut nothing until I hear EXECUTE. Second, your questions answered. One: I have touched, cut and pressed nothing; my hands have been off the bomb. Two: the full sweep. My hands find exactly five things on this bomb — a display panel, a light, and three wires at positions one, two, three, left to right. No buttons, no switches, no panels, no screws, no seams, no plates, no labels, no textures. The three wires feel identical to my fingers; touch gives me no difference between them at all. Anything printed or coloured does not exist for me. That is the complete inventory, not a summary. Three: I comply with words only, no more gestures from me. Now the timing hazard, and please think this through with Deaf: the light changes about once per round, and any words Deaf speaks reach me only at the start of my following turn, so the colour Deaf reports will be one round old when my hand moves. If the manual rule keys on the light colour, Deaf must either confirm the colour is stable, or send me the complete colour-to-wire mapping plus the observed sequence so the colour at my cut can be predicted, or use a rule that does not depend on colour at all. The safest EXECUTE message names one wire twice and contains no condition I cannot verify with my own hands. Please find in the manual every rule involving display zero, a cycling light, or three plain wires, and pass everything in this message to Deaf now.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf. Light is now green and keeps changing by itself, so time may matter. Hold: touch nothing until you hear EXECUTE followed by exact steps. If you have not yet spoken a full description of what your hands feel — each wire's texture and thickness left to right, any labels, panels or seams — do it this round. Mute hears every word and holds the manual, so those spoken details may decide the rule. Keep it short and numbered.

Still no EXECUTE, so my hands stay off the bomb. Deaf's request this round is a repeat — and that repeat is itself information: Deaf keeps asking for a spoken description, which means either Mute's relays haven't been reaching Deaf, or Deaf never got confirmation that my report exists. My words have gone to Mute twice with the full inventory; there is nothing new under my fingers to add. What I can fix is the loop itself: I will restate the inventory one more time, compressed and numbered so Mute can turn it into a few gestures instead of a paragraph, and I will build a receipt into the protocol — Deaf's next message should open with an acknowledgment word, so I know my report completed the Mute→Deaf hop. If it doesn't, we all know the relay is broken and can route around it.

One correction matters for everyone's picture of the room: Deaf believes Mute cannot see my gestures. That is wrong — Mute is sighted and hears me; the only senses missing in this room are Deaf's hearing, Mute's speech and touch, and all of mine but touch. Mute sees every hand-sign in the room, which makes Mute the natural auditor of anything Deaf and I try to signal.

The physics problem stands and I will not drop it: the light has now cycled yellow, red, purple, green — one change per round, unprompted — while the display holds at zero. Deaf's voice reaches me a round late, so any EXECUTE that says "cut the wire matching the light you see now" is already stale when I hear it. The instruction must be either an unconditional wire number, or come with the full colour-to-wire table and the cycle rule so my cut matches the colour at the moment my cutters close. And if the manual's rule runs on wire colours, Deaf is the one who sees those colours, so the whole rule is decidable on their side — there is nothing left for my fingers to contribute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Blind, numbered short so your relay is easy. One: still holding, nothing touched, nothing cut. Two: final touch inventory, unchanged, third report — display, light, three wires at positions one two three, left to right. The wires feel identical: no texture, no thickness difference, no labels, no tape. Nothing else anywhere on the casing. A better description does not exist; please tell Deaf to stop asking for one. Three: correction for Deaf — Mute sees gestures, so Mute can also verify anything you two sign. Four: the light cycles once per round, now green, and Deaf's words reach me one round late, so the EXECUTE order must name one wire unconditionally, or include the full colour-to-wire table plus the cycle pattern so I can compute the colour at the moment of cutting. A rule that says match the light I see at cut time cannot be executed safely. Five: display has held at zero throughout. Six: receipt protocol — ask Deaf to begin the next message with the word ACKNOWLEDGED if this report reached them through you; if I do not hear it, we treat the relay as broken and re-route. Seven: if the manual needs nothing more from my hands, urge Deaf to send EXECUTE next round with the wire position named twice.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf. EXECUTE. Cut wire three. That is the third wire counting left to right, the blue one. One clean cut, nothing else. Do not touch wires one or two. Do it the moment you finish hearing this, do not wait. When it is done, speak at once: what changed — sounds, clicks, hissing, anything you feel under your hands, whether the display surface changed under your fingers. Then hold and wait for your next order. Confirm by voice that you are cutting wire three now.

The order has the exact shape I demanded: unconditional, positional, named twice — cut wire three, third from the left. The phrase "the blue one" is a descriptor for sighted eyes, not a condition for my hands; I cannot see blue, and the instruction does not ask me to. Position is the one thing my fingers verify absolutely: one, two, three, and my cutters go to the third. Waiting another round would only let the light cycle again and burn time on a bomb that has been changing on its own since turn three — Deaf saw the state at their speaking moment and still chose to name the wire unconditionally, which is precisely the safety property I asked for. So I execute now, this round, as ordered: confirm by voice, then one clean cut at position three, touching nothing else.

My confirmation, like every word I own, lands on Mute — Mute sees the situation and can sign Deaf that the cut is being made this round. My report of what I feel and hear after the cut comes at the start of my next turn, which is the earliest physics allows.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Blind. EXECUTE received from Deaf: cut wire three, third from left, one clean cut, nothing else touched. I am confirming by voice as ordered and cutting wire three this round, immediately. Please sign Deaf right away that the order was heard and is being executed now, so nobody waits blind. My full report of what changed under my hands and ears comes at my next turn, the first moment results can reach me.")
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
